message.content:
The number of distinct legal positions that can arise in a game of chess is astronomically large.  In fact, the best estimates put it at roughly

**≈ 10⁴³ possible positions**

This figure is often called the *Shannon number* (after Claude Shannon), and it represents an estimate of the number of distinct board configurations that satisfy all of the rules of chess (piece placement, castling rights, en‑passant possibilities, etc.).  For comparison, the number of possible games (sequences of moves) is even larger—on the order of 10¹²⁰.
